subject: Recap: Reliability discussion — graceful degradation, fallbacks & SLOs
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Ellis <j.ellis@novaretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Reliability discussion — graceful degradation, fallbacks & SLOs

Hi Jordan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side + a few clarifying questions so we can scope the technical follow-up: 

Pain points you called out
- Recent user-facing incidents (search API outages) — 3 incidents in the last 6 months, longest outage ~22 minutes.
- Lack of graceful degradation: when the primary model pool is saturated, requests either queue >2s or fail hard.
- Manual region failover is slow and brittle; no automated fallback to smaller/cheap models.

Current stack (as discussed)
- In-house transformer serving on AWS (us-west-2) behind API Gateway -> autoscaling group of inference instances.
- Frontend rate limiter + Redis cache. No dedicated KV-cache for model state today.

Success criteria you mentioned
- Availability: >=99.95% for critical endpoints (search autocomplete / product ranking).
- P95 latency target: < 300ms for 1k-5k qps baseline (with spikes to 10k).
- Failover: automatic fallback to degraded mode within 60s when model pool is unhealthy; degraded mode should still return ranked results (best-effort) rather than errors.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Please share the incident postmortem(s) you referenced — we can ingest key root causes and map to fallbacks.
2) We’ll prepare a short runbook proposal: fallback model variants, regional routing policy, and an SLO draft for your critical routes.
3) Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week with Marcus to walk through your deployment topology and tagging strategy for traffic routing.

If I’ve missed anything, flag it. I’ll follow up with proposed times and attach a starter SLO template.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Recap: Reliability discussion — graceful degradation, fallbacks & SLOs

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear summary. That captures it well. A couple of clarifications and extra context: 

Incident details
- I’m attaching our internal incident summary (Prod-Incident-2025-Q2-summary.pdf). The biggest root cause across the incidents was overloaded GPUs causing inference worker crashes + a cascaded autoscaling lag.
- Our current policy is to retry 2x with exponential backoff; we see increased user friction when retries push effective latency >800ms.

Traffic shape and priority
- Two critical routes: /search/complete (high qps, can tolerate lower-quality fallbacks) and /order/intent (low qps, SLAs stricter).
- We’d prioritize availability for /order/intent and graceful degradation for /search/complete.

Constraints
- Compliance: all PII must stay in our VPC; we can evaluate Redwood Private if needed.
- Budget: we need a clear cost delta for dedicated capacity vs tapered fallback strategies.

We’re happy to schedule the deep-dive. Marcus’ calendar: he’s available Thu 6/26 or Tue 7/1 afternoons PT.

Jordan Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Nova Retail
j.ellis@novaretail.com

> - I’m attaching our internal incident summary (Prod-Incident-2025-Q2-summary.pdf). The biggest root cause across the incidents was overloaded GPUs causing inference worker crashes + a cascaded autoscaling lag.

Hi Jordan — thanks for the doc. A few technical notes from our side before the deep-dive: 

1) Fallback strategy options (high level)
- Model tiering: automatic fallback to a quantized smaller model in the same region when GPU memory pressure is detected. This preserves latency and avoids cross-region hops.
- Regional fallback: route to a secondary region (us-east-1) when whole-region capacity is constrained — adds cross-region latency but preserves availability.
- Graceful degradation mode: return cached or reranked results (prefix-KV cache + cheap embedding reranker) for high-qps routes like /search/complete.

2) Automated failover controls we recommend
- Health-based routing with 60s cooldown; ring-fenced reserve capacity for critical routes; and model-variant compatibility checks before traffic shift.

3) Metrics & SLOs to propose for the deep-dive
- Availability (error rate) per route, measured as 1 - green/total requests, with a target of 99.95% for /order/intent.
- P95 latency per route with a degraded-mode SLO (e.g., P95_degraded <= 450ms).
- Failover time objective: median failover < 60s, 95th percentile < 3m.

Next steps I’ll own
- Marcus and I will run a 30–45m technical session next week to map your routing tags and traffic priorities.
- I’ll prepare an initial runbook showing model-tiering rules and a cost estimate for reserved capacity vs on-demand fallbacks.

Thanks — Lauren

lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Thanks again — looking forward to the session.
